named_statements.label: Theorem 1
named_statements.claim: Uniform two-sided integer Sobolev bounds for one original Birkhoff map.

named_statements.label: Theorem 2
named_statements.claim: Uniform two-sided action-moment estimates, with the same constants as Theorem 1.

named_statements.label: Theorem 3
named_statements.claim: Weighted complex-neighborhood action bound and real Birkhoff target bound for all M1 weights.

named_statements.label: Corollary 1
named_statements.claim: Real-exponent Sobolev estimates and complex neighborhoods, including the endpoint one.

named_statements.label: Theorem 4
named_statements.claim: Absolutely convergent higher-action trace at every level k>=2 on the complex H^(k-1) source domain, with factor -1/(2i)^(k-1).

named_statements.label: Lemma 2
named_statements.claim: Joint and spectral analyticity of the Abelian differential, removability at closed gaps, and vanishing admissible endpoint and contour periods.

named_statements.label: Lemma 3
named_statements.claim: Joint analyticity, continuous endpoint extension, real logarithmic boundary values and zero-potential normalization of the primitive.

named_statements.label: Lemma 4
named_statements.claim: Convergent exterior Laurent expansion of the primitive for every complex finite-gap source, with independently defined Hamiltonian coefficients.
named_statements.qualification: At nonsmooth complex finite-gap sources, use the independently defined finite trace of original higher action contours as an explicit spectral extension of the hierarchy. Every coefficient is identified and physical Sobolev agreement is proved wherever the physical Riccati Hamiltonian is defined. The classical derivative-integral formula is not asserted at rough inputs.

named_statements.label: Theorem 5
named_statements.claim: Quadratic H1 spectral localization, two eigenvalues per tail cluster, explicit tail radius and central box.

named_statements.label: Lemma 5
named_statements.claim: Bounded shifted weighted Neumann operator with reversed shift and norm bound.

named_statements.label: Lemma 6
named_statements.claim: Explicit shifted weighted norm bound on the squared Neumann operator at every index and spectral strip point.

named_statements.label: Lemma 7
named_statements.claim: Equivalence of the physical eigenvalue equation and vanishing reduced two-by-two determinant at the stated threshold.

named_statements.label: Lemma 8
named_statements.claim: Equality of the two diagonal reduced-matrix entries.

named_statements.label: Lemma 9
named_statements.claim: Analyticity and uniform weighted estimates of the diagonal and off-diagonal reduced entries.

named_statements.label: Lemma 10
named_statements.claim: Exactly two reduced-determinant zeros, their quantitative disk localization and squared separation bound.

named_statements.label: Proposition 11
named_statements.claim: Weighted gap tail estimate and global complex-neighborhood gap bound.

named_statements.label: Proposition 12
named_statements.claim: High and low odd-level action comparisons from actual endpoint localization, retaining a mean-value point in the gap.

named_statements.label: Lemma 13
named_statements.claim: Weighted action moment bounded by the physical odd Hamiltonian plus an H1 remainder.

named_statements.label: Lemma 14
named_statements.claim: Uniform epsilon absorption for the absolute physical remainder integral and Hamiltonian bound with an L2-only lower term.

named_statements.label: Lemma 15
named_statements.claim: Energy-minus-mass-square kinetic action bound, weighted energy consequence and exact one-third H1 norm consequence.

named_statements.label: Lemma 16
named_statements.claim: All-index odd higher-action sum bounded by lower action moments with the stated exponents.
named_statements.proof_note: The exact printed statement is proved. A separate small zero-index argument repairs the use of the strict central hypothesis in the printed proof.

named_statements.label: Lemma 17
named_statements.claim: Uniform quantitative deleted-product bound on every high gap, including the finite head and infinite tail estimates.
named_statements.correction: Final chi constant 2048 replaces 512. The intermediate positive ratio is 128*(abs(n)+N+2/5)/(abs(n)-N+3/10), valid also at the inclusive boundary; this replaces the printed rational estimate.

named_statements.label: Proposition 18
named_statements.claim: Quadratic H1 action-to-gap estimate on the complex neighborhood.
named_statements.correction: Action-gap constant 4608 replaces 2048; the source remains complex H1 and the threshold is retained.

named_statements.label: Lemma 19
named_statements.claim: Local critical-point midpoint control near a collapsed complex gap and a uniform all-index neighborhood of every real source.

named_statements.label: Proposition 20
named_statements.claim: Joint analyticity of the primitive on the full disc-complement product, including continuity and weak analyticity across the collapsed-gap divisor.

named_statements.label: Lemma 21
named_statements.claim: All-order Riccati remainder polynomial: leading jet, total homogeneous weight, derivative count, highest jet order and field balance.
named_statements.regularity: Full complex H^(k-1), k=s+1; actual weak H^-1 density and physical remainder coefficients, as well as the polynomial and smooth statements.

named_statements.label: Corollary 22
named_statements.claim: One reduced polynomial per order on every real H^m source; exact leading kinetic energy, lower jets, homogeneous weight and field balance.
named_statements.regularity: Full real H^m; physical highest weak derivative and a single graded polynomial chosen before the source.

corrections_to_track.claim: Every higher level vanishes iff its gap is closed.
corrections_to_track.qualification: All levels vanish at collapsed gaps. The real-source converse is verified for odd levels; an unrestricted even-level converse is not claimed.

corrections_to_track.claim: H_k is the mean of phi_minus*u_k for every k>=1, with u_1=-phi_plus.
corrections_to_track.qualification: Use the positive mass H_1 from Section 2; the raw mean at level one has the opposite sign. Higher levels retain the literal Riccati mean and the trace factor -1/(2i)^(k-1).

corrections_to_track.claim: The introductory odd trace displays a sum only over n>=1.
corrections_to_track.qualification: Use all signed indices n in Z, as in the later trace formula and the checked original action trace. The displayed positive-only index was verified in the rendered PDF.

corrections_to_track.claim: Formula (1) prints a standard-root radicand with denominator 4*(tau_n-lambda).
corrections_to_track.qualification: The standard-root radicand requires 4*(tau_n-lambda)^2. The missing square was verified in the rendered PDF. The existing normalized standard root uses the squared denominator.

corrections_to_track.claim: The central comparison in the proof of Lemma 16 is applied to index zero even when the potential is small.
corrections_to_track.qualification: Use the first-action estimate on the entire zero gap when P<=1/4; otherwise use the central third-action estimate. This directly proves the printed final bound without changing its mass exponents.

corrections_to_track.claim: Lemma 17 gives chi constant 512 and a rational intermediate bound.
corrections_to_track.qualification: Use constant 2048 and the positive ratio recorded in the named-statement entry. Proposition 18 then uses constant 4608.
Use the actual denominator kernel, whose squared double sum is <=16/(1+abs(n))^2.
Both diagonal expressions use (I-T_n^2)^-1. The intermediate bound uses 2*norm(first)*norm(second)/(1+abs(n)), followed by 2ab<=a^2+b^2; do not assert each printed separate component-square bound.
The displayed complex difference is 2*i*Im(lambda), rather than 2*Im(lambda). The actual spectral-height estimate is proved directly.
Keep the original source cutoff N distinct from period-two cutoff 2N. Horizontal packing and spectral height replace the arbitrary-isolating-disc diameter shortcut.
Use natural integer multiplicities of the actual polynomial support instead of unsupported half-integer multiplicities.
In the repeated-index display remove the unused second index from the residual product restriction.
Use i<m for the supremum estimate; the L2 estimate allows i<=m. The printed supremum endpoint is not asserted.
Replace the intermediate numerator D-4 by D-2; the final printed beta is retained.
The physical norm split uses 2^(2m-1), replacing the printed 2^(m-1). Epsilon is rescaled before this split.
With physical period one and the sampled weight w(2n), the exact Abel strip width is a/pi. The printed narrower-strip statement is retained only in the forward direction.
Restore the omitted square in the printed denominator. The collapsed root is exactly tau-z, with its normalization fixed before any action is defined.
Use the analytically filled quotient at a collapsed gap, and magnitudes for complex inequalities; do not interpret a raw 0/0 as the normalized value.

Use the directly proved finite-core and exterior budgets rather than asserting every numerical inequality in the printed e^2 chain. Original signed indices, source norms and omitted factor are retained.

Spectral continuity constructs the required common neighborhood. The comparison is not inferred solely from arbitrary disjoint isolating discs. The positive finite core uses -N<m<N and includes boundary modes in the exterior budget.
Retain 1+P_w^2 and the inclusive boundary. The printed tail expression that drops the additive one is not used.
The finite central set is empty at cutoff zero. Choose N=floor(8*P_w^2), allowing equality in N<=8*P_w^2.
The near-zero quadratic factor is the original weighted norm P_w, not the smaller H1 norm printed there.

corrections_to_track.claim: The printed affine spectral curve is stated as a subset of C.
corrections_to_track.qualification: Use the actual ambient complex plane squared C x C. The two coordinates, Jacobian and complex manifold atlas are constructed explicitly.

corrections_to_track.claim: All-order Hamiltonian coefficients of Lemma 4 at nonsmooth complex finite-gap sources.

The actual Laurent coefficients equal this trace and it agrees with independently defined physical Riccati Hamiltonians on every admissible complex Sobolev domain. No smoothness follows from complex finite-gap data, and classical derivative products are not assigned to rough inputs.

corrections_to_track.claim: The unreduced odd-Hamiltonian display before Corollary 22, with q_(2m) fixed by Lemma 21.
